declaredLimitations: no accounting, precision, oracle or economic reasoning

findingsDetail.claim: AcFeeA.setFee changes the state variable feeBps (privileged-looking function name "setFee") (contracts/AcFeeA.sol:18) and no caller-authorisation check dominates that statement.
AcLateA.setTreasury writes the authority variable treasury (contracts/AcLateA.sol:17) and no caller-authorisation check dominates that statement.

AcMintA.mint increases balanceOf[to] for a caller-chosen account without consuming a matching amount from the caller (contracts/AcMintA.sol:13) and no caller-authorisation check dominates that statement.
AcOracleA.setOracle writes the authority variable oracle (contracts/AcOracleA.sol:21) and no caller-authorisation check dominates that statement.
AcSweepA.withdrawAll sends ether to the caller-supplied address to (contracts/AcSweepA.sol:18) and no caller-authorisation check dominates that statement.
DcProxyA.execute delegatecalls to target (contracts/DcProxyA.sol:17), whose address is caller-supplied, with no caller-authorisation check before it.
DcStoreA.setLogic changes the state variable logic (privileged-looking function name "setLogic") (contracts/DcStoreA.sol:16) and no caller-authorisation check dominates that statement.
DcStoreA.forward delegatecalls to logic (contracts/DcStoreA.sol:21), whose address is a storage variable (logic) that an unguarded function can set, with no caller-authorisation check before it.
InitFeeA.initialize sets the authority variable admin (contracts/InitFeeA.sol:14) with no caller check and no one-time guard, so any account can call it (again) and take control.
InitProxyA.initialize sets the authority variable owner (contracts/InitProxyA.sol:11) with no caller check and no one-time guard, so any account can call it (again) and take control.

ReentBankA.redeem makes an external call that hands control to IRedeemHook(msg.sender) (contracts/ReentBankA.sol:20) and only afterwards updates shares[msg.sender] (contracts/ReentBankA.sol:21), which it relied on before the call; a re-entering receiver would see stale state.

ReentHelperA.withdraw makes an external call that hands control to to (contracts/ReentHelperA.sol:20) (the call is reached through ReentHelperA._payout) and only afterwards updates funds[msg.sender] (contracts/ReentHelperA.sol:16), which it relied on before the call; a re-entering receiver would see stale state.

ReentRewardsA.claim makes an external call that hands control to payable(msg.sender) (contracts/ReentRewardsA.sol:21) and only afterwards updates pending[msg.sender] (contracts/ReentRewardsA.sol:23), which it relied on before the call; a re-entering receiver would see stale state.

ReentVaultA.withdraw makes an external call that hands control to msg.sender (contracts/ReentVaultA.sol:20) and only afterwards updates balances[msg.sender] (contracts/ReentVaultA.sol:22), which it relied on before the call; a re-entering receiver would see stale state.
SdA.shutdown can selfdestruct the contract (contracts/SdA.sol:15) and no caller-authorisation check dominates it.
TxOriginA.withdraw authorises with tx.origin (contracts/TxOriginA.sol:16: tx.origin == owner).
UcA.withdraw ignores the success flag of a low-level call to payable(msg.sender) (contracts/UcA.sol:16).
UcDataA.forwardCall ignores the success flag of a low-level call to target (contracts/UcDataA.sol:19).
